summary: The Genomic Answers for Children's Health Act of 2026 amends the Social Security Act to clarify that whole genome sequencing and whole exome sequencing are covered under the Medicaid program for children with certain medical needs. The bill mandates separate payments for these tests, requires outreach and education efforts, and calls for federal reports on implementation, payment amounts, and health outcomes starting January 1, 2027.

affected_groups.effect: Gain explicit Medicaid coverage for whole genome and whole exome sequencing when ordered as a first-tier test for suspected genetic disorders, rare diseases, or conditions of unknown origin.
affected_groups.group: Children on Medicaid with certain medical needs

affected_groups.effect: Can order whole genome and whole exome sequencing for eligible children within their scope of practice under State law.
Must provide separate payment for whole genome and whole exome sequencing and participate in federal outreach and reporting efforts.
affected_groups.group: State Medicaid programs and managed care organizations

key_provisions: Clarifies that whole genome sequencing and whole exome sequencing are covered under Medicaid for children suspected of having a genetic disorder, rare disease, or health condition of unknown origin when ordered by a qualified provider.

Includes within the definition of sequencing the analysis, interpretation, and data report, as well as testing of first-degree biological relatives if it primarily benefits the individual's diagnosis or treatment.
Requires that payment for whole genome and whole exome sequencing be made separately and not bundled into payments for other medical assistance.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to convene national organizations and stakeholders to identify implementation challenges and best practices regarding prior authorization and administrative requirements.
Requires the Secretary to conduct outreach to raise awareness of screening, diagnostic, and treatment services under Medicaid.
Mandates that the Department of Health and Human Services publish a public report within two years on state payment amounts, number of children served, health outcomes, and services provided.
Directs the Comptroller General to collect feedback, assess impacts of prior authorization and workforce challenges, and make recommendations within two years.
